findings.function: updateRewardTokens, pause, unpause, updateFeeReceiver and every 'restricted' function (6 lines; also in 12 other contracts)
findings.decompiled: static call authority.canCall(address _src, address _dst, bytes4 _sig) with: args Bytes(28, uint128(caller >> 32)), Bytes(4, uint32(caller)), this.address, call.func_hash
findings.issue: The first argument, msg.sender, is printed as two slices of caller (28 + 4 bytes) because the word was stored across the selector's 4-byte offset.
findings.rule: Adjacent pieces Bytes(28, x >> 32), Bytes(4, uint32(x)) of one value x that together cover a 32-byte argument are x (here caller); merge slices of the same source before decoding arguments.

findings.issue: length >> 128 is printed as a member 'field_128' of the slot holding the array length, which reads like a struct field.
findings.rule: Print a shift of a whole-slot value that the storage analysis typed as a scalar (here an array length) as a shift ('checkpoints[account].length >> 128'), and use field_N only for slots typed as packed structs.
